title: Black pepper and bergamot soy candle
subtitle: A warm, spiced container candle for living rooms
excerpt: A container soy candle blending a black pepper and amber fragrance oil with bergamot essential oil. Warm and slightly spiced, with a bright citrus top note. Makes one 200 ml jar candle.
sourceNotes: Soy wax fragrance binding and pour-temperature reference: general candlemaking formulation. Bergamot essential oil phototoxicity note (not relevant for a candle product): IFRA guidelines. Black pepper and amber fragrance oil: IFRA-rated candle-grade fragrance oil.

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 jar candle (~200 ml jar, ~35 burn hours)
recipe.batchNotes: Make four or five jars in one session.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure one week before first burn.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years unlit in a cool, dark place. The fragrance oil is stable for 18 months in the wax.

glossaryTerms.definition: The resting period after a candle is poured and set, during which the fragrance oil fully bonds with the wax matrix. Most container soy candles need at least one week of cure time for the best scent throw on first burn. Lighting too early produces a flat, weak scent.

content.text: A spiced soy candle with a warm, slightly masculine character. The black pepper and amber fragrance oil gives a deep, resinous base; bergamot essential oil (added at 2% of wax weight alongside the fragrance oil) lifts it with a citrus brightness. The
is the step most beginners skip; one week makes a real difference to the scent throw on the first burn.
Bergamot essential oil is toxic to cats. Never leave a burning candle unattended.

items.prepNote: black pepper and amber fragrance oil; 5% of wax weight
2% of wax weight; adds a citrus top note; add at 60°C alongside the fragrance oil
pre-tabbed cotton wick for a 200 ml jar

content.text: Warm the jar. Fix the wick in the centre. Melt the soy wax to liquid, then cool to 60°C. Add the fragrance oil and bergamot essential oil together at 60°C and stir for one minute. Pour into the jar and leave overnight. Trim the wick to 5 mm once set. Cure for one week.
Allow the melt pool to reach the jar edge on the first burn before extinguishing. Trim the wick to 5 mm before each subsequent burn.
Two years unlit in a cool, dark place.
